messages:
vikram: Heads up — proposing a conservative 'staircase' ramp for model v3 -> v4 swaps where we limit any step to 5% and hold for 10m with SLO checks.
maria: Can you outline the SLO checks? latency, p95 error-rate?
vikram: yes: p50/p95 latency, inferred token-time, 5xx rate, and a small prompt-regression eval run (10k samples) — fail if p95 increases >20% or 5xx >0.2%.
jamie: 5% steps every 10m feels slow for high-traffic customers. can we have an aggressive ladder for dedicated pools? :thinking:
vikram: Agreed. plan: two profiles — "conservative" (default) for hosted & sensitive tenants, and "aggressive" for dedicated high-commit customers. Console defaults to conservative.
maria: How do we express that in the rollout API? show example payload?
vikram: pasted config snippet: 
```
rollout: {
  strategy: \"staircase\",
  steps: [5,10,20,30,35],
  hold_minutes: 10,
  slo_checks: [{metric:\"p95_latency_ms\",threshold:1.2,operator:\"lt\"},{metric:\"error_rate_5xx\",threshold:0.002,operator:\"lt\"}],
  fallback: {immediate: false, rollback_window_minutes:30}
}
```
jamie: nit: thresholds should be relative delta not absolute; prefer factor e.g. 1.2 rather than ms.
vikram: right — the p95 entry is a multiplicative factor vs baseline. updated in snippet.
kai: telemetry note — we need cohort-level delta metrics per step and a sampled replay to detect hallucination/regression. will need eval hooks and a small golden-prompt set run.
maria: console UX: show expected throughput and estimated cost delta per step. customers asked for a cost projection before committing steps.
vikram: also add a 'safety hold' button in the UI to pause the rollout and require manual acknowledgement if SLOs failed or if an operator flags it.
jamie: we need route-level targeting: ability to apply percentage only to specific routes (search vs summarization).
vikram: yes — include routeSelectors and cohort filters in the API. enforce that sum(traffic_splits) <= 100 per route/global.
maria: warmup idea — pre-warm KV and prefix caches and prime tokenizers. add an optional pre-warm boolean that triggers background synthetic traffic.
kai: +1. pre-warm should also warm up tensor kernels on GPU (spin up a tiny warmup pool) to avoid first-step spikes.
vikram: autoscaler interplay: bind a minimum reserved capacity for the canary so autoscaler doesn't scale to zero and cause 503s. add resourceReserves in rollout config.
jamie: fallback strategy: prefer degrade-to-multiple-variants (eg split across fallback-tier models) rather than single full rollback, unless catastrophic error.
maria: agree. also tag telemetry with rollout_id, step_index, cohort_id to reason about regressions later.
vikram: also provide a dry-run simulation mode that replays historical traces with proposed splits and projects SLO impact. helpful for sales/SEs.
jamie: auto-promote policy? can we auto-advance after N consecutive passing steps?
vikram: yes — add parameter consecutive_successes (default 2 for aggressive, 3 for conservative).
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: canary-rollout-v4 config by vikram. status: pending-approval.
vikram: I'll draft the API PR and console mocks. want input on UX phrasing for 'hold' vs 'manual pause'.
maria: prefer 'pause and require acknowledgement' copy. plumb an audit log entry when operator resumes.
kai: add telemetry event when pre-warm completes and when each step starts/stops. keep sample size per step configurable.
jamie: let's make sure default conservative profile is documented and surfaced in the quickstart so small teams don't accidentally pick aggressive.
vikram: noted. will add docs + tests. tagging eng-platform to pick this up for next sprint.
maria: lgtm, please assign and include an RFC with the API contract.
vikram: thanks — I'll circulate RFC tomorrow and drop console mocks in #design for quick feedback.
